data.content_ref: inline:The target misappropriates Popper's propensity interpretation by committing a category error. Popper developed the propensity interpretation specifically as an account of single-case probabilities in physical chance set-ups (e.g., quantum-mechanical experiments); propensity is a property of the *experimental arrangement*, not of *theories*. The target's mechanism attributes propensity to 'the theory relative to the world,' treating a theory as though it were a physical object with dispositional properties. This is conceptually incoherent: theories are abstract entities, not physical systems that can bear objective dispositional properties 'relative to the world.' Furthermore, the target's own countercondition — 'Must accept propensity as a real, albeit unprovable, feature of the universe' — demands an unfalsifiable metaphysical commitment, which directly contradicts Popper's demarcation criterion that genuine scientific claims must be falsifiable. The target thus attempts to rescue Popper's position by importing a metaphysical assumption Popper himself would classify as non-scientific.
